title: (No AI) Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
author: Emma Roth
content:
![A person holding an iPhone 18 Pro phone showing the lock screen.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/DSC04239.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That's according to [a job listing](https://jobs.apple.com/en-us/details/200695488-0836/senior-engineering-manager-agentic-ai-proactive?team=SFTWR) spotted [by _Bloomberg_](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/apple-is-working-on-ai-agent-for-device-control-apps-browsing-and-coding), which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

An AI agent from Apple would put the iPhone maker in the running to compete with the likes of [Meta's Muse](https://www.theverge.com/column/999999/optimizer-meta-muse-ai-cute), [OpenAI's Dots](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1002033/openai-dots-launch-muse-competitor), [Anthropic's Duet](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1032518/claude-duet-ai-agent-hands-on), and [Google's Tasks](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1035756/google-spark-ai-tasks-free). Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while [Google just started letting Gemini](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1037902/google-gemini-macos-ai-computer-use) do the same.

Apple began rolling out it …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1038227/apple-ai-agent-engineer-job-listing)

title: (No AI) A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
author: Ellen Thomas
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/gettyimages-2305716823.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on November 18, 2026 in New York City. | Image: Getty Images

"We've got this," Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company's third quarter earnings call.

By Thursday, the company's [stock price](https://investor.nvidia.com/stock-info/stock-quote-and-chart/default.aspx) was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia's biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share - 34 percent higher than expected.

Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than [doubled](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1036032/nvidia-q3-2027-jensen-huang) from the same period …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1038063/nvidia-stock-market-price-earnings)

title: (No AI) The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
dc:creator: Amy Chang Chien
content: In Taiwan, some food vendors are distancing themselves from Nvidia’s former CEO. Others stand by him. “It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire,” says one shop owner.
